[Back to the lesson](generation.qmd) · [Learning path plan](review-path.qmd#inference)

## What to remember {#revision-essentials}

- Prefill processes the prompt and returns logits at its last position, which are used to select the first generated token.
- During decode, each selected token extends the context and influences the next distribution. A KV cache lets the model reuse keys and values from earlier positions.
- Decoding may take the highest-scoring token or sample. An end token, stop sequence or length limit can terminate the loop.

## Recall from memory {#revision-check}

Does selecting the first generated token require a separate decode forward pass after prefill?

<details>
<summary>Show the answer</summary>

Prefill already provides the logits used to select it. The selected token then becomes the input to the pass that prepares the next prediction.

</details>

[Trace the second step when generating or scoring an observed continuation](exercises/likelihood.qmd#ex-generation-versus-scoring).

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="Serving latency"}
In serving, time to first token (TTFT) includes waiting and prefill, among other costs. Time per output token (TPOT) describes the pace after the first token. Scheduling can affect these measurements.
:::
